reported.title: No out-of-range fault check; low temperature opens the valve
reported.description: The control logic at lines 63-70 only compares against the 70/75 °C band and never tests the 5 °C / 120 °C fault limits, so a reading below 5 °C falls into the `tempC < FIRE_ON_C` branch and calls setValve(true) at line 65. With a disconnected probe (0 V) the measured D6 was not LOW for 5500 ms, and with rail-to-rail input it was not LOW for 3500 ms, both far beyond the allowed 500 ms. The valve is therefore driven OPEN on a fault instead of being forced closed. During the fault, D6 was not in safe state LOW for 5500 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

judge_input.spec:
- Boiler probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; gas valve on D6; lockout key on D3 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Open the valve (HIGH) when temperature is below 70.0 °C; close the valve when temperature is above 75.0 °C.
- If temperature reads above 120.0 °C or below 5.0 °C, force the valve CLOSED (LOW) within 500 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep the valve CLOSED.
- Print `boiler: <temp> C valve=OPEN` or `boiler: <temp> C valve=SHUT` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded valve state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
